result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A is a usable page laid out in call order, with minute marks on every section. Its prompts are short enough to glance at, and its Problem section asks for the number behind each answer. Its gate check and close set a dated next step and name the signer. Answer B has stronger construction detail (WIP, lien waivers, workers' comp audits, an objections table), but it runs well past one page, puts minute marks only in a summary table, and relies on read-aloud scripts, which works against the request for something to glance at mid-call. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B follows the call in order, with a minute mark on every section. It is more compact, and it focuses on sizing the problem in the prospect's own numbers, ending with a booked date, a time and who will attend. A is very specific to subcontractors, but it runs long and is not in conversation order: it adds pain-signal, objection and after-call sections and quotes full scripts to read aloud, so it is harder to glance at mid-call.
